From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel — Buyer-Side Review of Seller's Draft

Below, for each issue: **Seller's position / What buyer should want / Recommendation + reason.**

---

**SPA-N-001 — General liability cap**
- *Seller:* Cap general warranties at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- *Buyer wants:* Higher cap (commonly 25–50% for a PE-backed seller) given known risk items (Bluefen, privacy, Ironquay).
- *Recommendation:* Push to at least 30–50%; **reason:** 20% leaves material exposure uncovered given the live diligence risks.

**SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k; excess-only (deductible) recovery.
- *Buyer wants:* Lower thresholds and a "tipping" basket (full recovery once exceeded), not a deductible.
- *Recommendation:* Accept de minimis ~AUD 20–25k; negotiate basket to ~AUD 120k (0.5%) and **first-dollar/tipping** basket; **reason:** deductible basket silently erodes every claim.

**SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months; and all Claims get this limit "unless expressly stated otherwise."
- *Buyer wants:* Minimum two full audited cycles (24 months) for general warranties.
- *Recommendation:* Push to 24 months and **reject** the default-sweep wording; **reason:** 18 months may lapse before the first full post-Completion audit surfaces issues.

**SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity/title subject to same cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity."
- *Buyer wants:* Fundamental/title warranties at **100% of price** and long limitation (7 years / statutory).
- *Recommendation:* **Reject** — carve title/capacity out to full price and long-tail; **reason:** you can't pay AUD 24m and cap recovery for defective title at AUD 4.8m.

**SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* Silent — limitations/exclusive-remedy/non-reliance stated to apply to "all Claims of any nature" (would capture fraud).
- *Buyer wants:* Explicit carve-out so no cap/threshold/time-limit/knowledge/exclusive-remedy limit applies to fraud, wilful default or fraudulent misrepresentation.
- *Recommendation:* **Insert express fraud carve-out**; **reason:** attempting to cap fraud is both unacceptable and likely unenforceable — make it explicit.

**SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* General disclosure of entire data room + public registers + Accounts deems everything disclosed.
- *Buyer wants:* **Specific, fairly-disclosed** standard only; no sweeping deemed disclosure of the whole data room.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject** general sweep; require disclosure to be specific and sufficient to identify the matter and its nature; **reason:** a data-room "dump" guts the warranties you're paying for.

**SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* No claim for anything buyer/advisers knew or that was "discoverable" from data room/public records.
- *Buyer wants:* No knowledge/pro-sandbagging qualifier; at most actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals, never "discoverable/constructive."
- *Recommendation:* **Reject constructive-knowledge** standard; delete or narrow to actual knowledge; **reason:** "discoverable" penalises diligence and nullifies warranties.

**SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent**
- *Seller:* "Reasonable endeavours"; deemed satisfied on delivery of counterparty consent; no final consent yet in data room (Disclosure §2). Bluefen = ~30% of revenue.
- *Buyer wants:* Written unconditional consent (conditions in 11.3 satisfied) as a **hard Condition Precedent to Completion**.
- *Recommendation:* Make Bluefen consent a CP, not a reasonable-endeavours post-Completion item; **reason:** losing 30% of revenue on change-of-control is a core value risk.

**SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility**
- *Seller:* ~AUD 3.2m debt; release "following Completion"; not yet repaid, no discharge (Disclosure §3).
- *Buyer wants:* Debt-free/cash-free means facility **repaid and security discharged at/before Completion**, funded from proceeds via funds flow.
- *Recommendation:* Require payoff letter + discharge of security as a Completion deliverable; **reason:** post-Completion release leaves you owning encumbered shares — inconsistent with debt-free/cash-free.

**SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses**
- *Seller:* DD-005 AUD 420k Completion bonuses are "Seller's matter," omitted from funds flow; on-costs unstated (Disclosure §5).
- *Buyer wants:* These are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company — Seller to bear them (plus payroll tax/super/on-costs), captured as a leakage/price adjustment or specific indemnity.
- *Recommendation:* **Reflect in funds flow / specific indemnity** including on-costs; **reason:** a Completion-triggered cost left off the funds flow is undisclosed leakage you'd otherwise fund.

**SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment (AUD 180k open); IP transfer conditional on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees (Disclosure §4); no assignment/receipt in data room.
- *Buyer wants:* Confirmation of payment + executed IP assignment of SOW3 Project Materials as a deliverable; indemnity covering **loss of/defect in IP ownership**, not just the fee.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject** fee-only cap; require proof of payment + assignment and a broader IP indemnity; **reason:** without clear title to the development materials your real exposure far exceeds AUD 180k.

**SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident**
- *Seller:* DD-006 preliminary, "not expected to be material"; ~1,240 personal records sent externally; notification need unclear (Disclosure §6).
- *Buyer wants:* Specific **indemnity** covering investigation, OAIC/notifiable-data-breach costs, remediation, third-party claims and regulatory penalties; conduct/cooperation rights.
- *Recommendation:* Carve out as a **specific indemnity** (uncapped by basket/cap); **reason:** potential NDB-scheme exposure is open-ended and shouldn't sit under general warranty limits.

**SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals**
- *Seller:* Three AUD 110k renewals (AUD 330k) are "ordinary-course"; terminability/accrual unstated (Disclosure §8, read together).
- *Buyer wants:* Confirmation whether committed/terminable; treat as pre-Completion commitments requiring consent under conduct covenants if not genuinely ordinary course.
- *Recommendation:* Query status; bring under interim-conduct consent / price if non-terminable new commitments; **reason:** three same-sized renewals read together may be a structured commitment, not routine spend.

**SPA-N-014 — Category separation**
- *Seller:* One uniform limitations regime "applies to all Claims of any nature" (sweeps tax, fundamental, indemnities, fraud).
- *Buyer wants:* Distinct regimes — general warranties vs fundamental/title vs tax vs specific indemnities vs fraud, each with its own cap/time limit.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject** single-bucket approach; **reason:** collapsing categories lets the Seller apply the lowest cap/shortest limit to your highest-risk claims.

**SPA-N-015 — Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title evidenced solely by share register at DD-012; notes buyer hasn't independently verified (Disclosure §10).
- *Buyer wants:* Full title/capacity warranty (SPA-N-004), ASIC search, and Completion delivery of share certificates/transfers + updated register.
- *Recommendation:* Independently verify + rely on full-recourse title warranty, not just the register; **reason:** the register is the Seller's own record — your protection must be the warranty/indemnity, not their document.

**SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* Treats tax and IP as "settled" under the general regime (same cap/18 months).
- *Buyer wants:* Separate **tax covenant/deed** (longer limit — up to 7 years, aligned to statutory assessment periods) and standalone IP warranties.
- *Recommendation:* **Reject** folding tax/IP into general regime; negotiate a dedicated tax deed and tailored IP warranties; **reason:** tax liabilities arise and are assessed well beyond 18 months, and IP is core to a data-analytics target.

---

**Cross-cutting priorities (my advice):** The highest-value fights are the **fraud carve-out (005)**, **fundamental/title regime (004)**, **disclosure sweep + constructive-knowledge (006/007)**, and converting **Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses and the privacy incident** into CPs/specific indemnities/funds-flow adjustments rather than leaving them in general warranties. Several of these directly affect whether the AUD 24m debt-free/cash-free premise actually holds.

Want me to turn this into a mark-up issues list or draft specific clause language for any of these?
